[THOUGHT] Intermittent, colicky flank pain in a 31-year-old with no lower urinary symptoms most commonly suggests nephrolithiasis; microscopic hematuria on urinalysis would strongly support that. A single, noninvasive test (urinalysis with microscopy) is high-yield and will help decide need for imaging.

This single imaging test will likely provide the diagnostic evidence needed.

Other causes of renal cysts are less likely given the bilateral enlargement and presentation. No further tests are required to state the single most likely diagnosis.

[DIAGNOSIS] Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD).
